note: A world_buildings fragment (src/buildings.cpp): res/systems/ksp_system.json names it under "world_buildings_files" and the loader merges these entries into its own "world_buildings". Hand-authored -- utils/gen_systems.py emits only the reference, never this table, so regenerating the system JSON cannot clobber a coordinate; tests/test_buildings.cpp pins what reaches the game. lat_deg/lon_deg are DEGREES, lon east-positive, in the BODY's own equirect frame (equirect.h), so the same numbers on two bodies are the same place on each of them. Each BODY's default site is the first VAB_LAUNCH_PAD for that body (find_launch_site filters by body), and merged fragments come before a system's inline world_buildings -- so this table picks Kerbin's, Moho's and Duna's defaults. Kerbin's polar pad is gone entirely (#1063), so that order rule is pinned by the synthetic inline row in tests/test_buildings.cpp rather than by shipped data. moho_pad and duna_pad sit at Kerbin's coordinates: placeholders so off-world launches are reachable, not placed against any survey. ksc_runway IS placed against a survey (tmp/runway_probe.cpp, reports/runway-wheels2026_11_14): a 900x30 m footprint with 0.56 m of relief, 2.7 km from the pad. It carries VAB_LAUNCH_PAD so the picker/map/recovery see it, plus RUNWAY which selects the horizontal spawn pose; it sits AFTER main_space_port so the default site is unchanged. heading_deg spins the mesh's long axis (local +X); at this site faceAlong's axis pick lands X=east, so heading 5 deg matches the survey's east-based azimuth -- at another site that correspondence can flip (the spawn reads the actual building basis, so ship and mesh always agree).
